prompt.context: Mr. Krabs, the owner of the restaurant 'The Krunchy Krab', has a predicament. The Krunchy Krab has reigned as king of the Martini Bottom casual restaurant market for quite some time, however, their primary competitor, 'The Clam Bucket', which is run by Mr. Krabs' arch nemesis, Plankton, has been rapidly stealing market share from the Krunchy Krab for the last few years. Krabs has hired your consulting firm to figure out how to solidify its place as the dominant player in the market. Last year, the Krunchy Krab brought in $500K in revenue.
prompt.question: What should Mr. Krabs do to improve sales this year?

clarifying_info.q: What products does the Krunchy Krab currently sell?
clarifying_info.a: The Krunchy Krab currently sells only 1 product, the 'Krunchy Patty', which is a 100% lean beef burger.

clarifying_info.q: How much revenue did the Clam Bucket bring in last year?
clarifying_info.a: Last year, the Clam Bucket brought in $400K in revenue.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the total market?
clarifying_info.a: The Krunchy Krab competes in the casual restaurant market in Martini Bottom which is a $1.5M market located just outside the U.S.
The casual restaurant market is fairly concentrated in Martini Bottom — in addition to the Clam Bucket and the Krunchy Krab, there are a few other smaller competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Why has the Clam Bucket been stealing market share?
clarifying_info.a: We don't have any information as to why the Clam Bucket has been stealing market share at the moment.

clarifying_info.q: What is Mr. Krabs' specific sales goal?
clarifying_info.a: Mr. Krabs is eager for retirement, so he wants quick results. The primary objective is for the Krunchy Krab to increase annual sales to $750K THIS year (a 50% share of last year's total market size).

clarifying_info.q: Can the Krunchy Krab acquire more than one restaurant?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they are welcome to choose more than one option.

clarifying_info.q: What is the capital budget available for acquisitions?
clarifying_info.a: Mr. Krabs estimates that the Krunchy Krab has $400K in its capital budget which they are willing to spend toward M&A activity.

exhibits.shows: A table listing four potential acquisition targets with their purchase price, annual revenue, and synergy potential rating.

data.note: Mr. Krabs estimates that the Krunchy Krab has $400K in its capital budget which they are willing to spend toward M&A activity.

exhibits.title: Strategic Initiatives
exhibits.shows: A chart comparing four potential strategic initiatives on two dimensions: Potential Annual Revenues ($000s) on the y-axis and Expected % of Revenue Captured This Year on the x-axis. Four initiatives are plotted: Krunchy Patty/Dutchman Fries Combo, Patrick Pizza Saturday Special, Bubble Ads Promotional Plan, and Krab Kard Rewards Program.

framework: Organic Growth — Same Products, Same Markets: improve customer experience, build referral/rewards programs, hire more staff for peak times, increase hours of operation, adjust pricing
Organic Growth — Same Products, New Markets: increase marketing efforts, expand geographically into new regions
Organic Growth — New Products, New Markets: introduce new product lines (e.g., hot dogs, fries, veggie burgers)
Inorganic Growth: acquire a competitor to quickly gain market share and generate synergies
Interviewer should steer away from a pure profitability (revenue/cost) framework — the focus should be on growing market share and sales
Given Mr. Krabs' short-term retirement timeline, inorganic growth via acquisition is the best path; nudge toward this if the candidate does not identify it

questions.prompt: Which acquisition target(s) would you recommend the Krunchy Krab acquire to meet the $750K sales goal, given a $400K capital budget?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recall the $250K revenue gap needed ($750K target minus $500K current). They should evaluate all combinations of acquisitions that stay within the $400K budget and maximize added revenue. No single restaurant achieves $250K in added revenue within budget. The best combination is Flying Dutchman Fries ($225K price, $150K revenue) + Patrick's Pizza ($75K price, $75K revenue) = $300K total price (within budget) and $225K added revenue — the closest to $250K within budget. Both also carry medium or high synergy potential. Candidate should note that no combination fully reaches $250K, leaving a $25K gap to be addressed through synergies.

math.setup: Need $250K additional revenue to reach $750K target. Capital budget = $400K. Evaluate combinations within budget.
steps: Sandy's Steaks alone: $500K price > $400K budget — ruled out
Squiddy's Sandwiches alone: $375K price, adds only $125K revenue — gap of $125K remains
Flying Dutchman Fries alone: $225K price, adds $150K revenue — gap of $100K remains
Patrick's Pizza alone: $75K price, adds $75K revenue — gap of $175K remains
Flying Dutchman Fries + Patrick's Pizza: $225K + $75K = $300K total price (within $400K budget), $150K + $75K = $225K added revenue — gap of $25K remains
Squiddy's Sandwiches + Patrick's Pizza: $375K + $75K = $450K > $400K budget — ruled out
Flying Dutchman Fries + Patrick's Pizza is the only feasible combination that gets closest to the target
Optional Price/Revenue ratio check: Patrick's Pizza = $75K/$75K = 1.0x (best), Flying Dutchman Fries = $225K/$150K = 1.5x (second best)
math.answer: Acquire Flying Dutchman Fries ($225K) and Patrick's Pizza ($75K) for a combined cost of $300K, adding $225K in revenue. This leaves a $25K synergy gap to close.

questions.prompt: What revenue synergies can the Krunchy Krab create between itself, Flying Dutchman Fries, and Patrick's Pizza to capture the remaining $25K?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm revenue synergy strategies across pricing and volume levers. Strong answers will cover bundling/combo deals, shared marketing, new complementary products, promotions, and loyalty programs. After brainstorming, show Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 2, which single strategic initiative would you recommend to capture the remaining $25K needed?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate expected revenue captured this year for each initiative (Potential Annual Revenue x % Captured This Year) and identify which clears the $25K threshold. The Bubble Ads Promotional Plan is the correct answer: $650K x 4% = $26K, just exceeding the $25K gap. Candidate should also note that Krunchy Patty/Dutchman Fries Combo yields $100K x 20% = $20K (insufficient), Patrick Pizza Saturday Special yields $500K x 4% = $20K (insufficient), and Krab Kard Rewards Program yields $800K x 2% = $16K (insufficient).

math.setup: Expected revenue this year = Potential Annual Revenue x Expected % of Revenue Captured This Year. Need at least $25K.
steps: Krunchy Patty / Dutchman Fries Combo: $100K x 20% = $20K — insufficient
Patrick Pizza Saturday Special: $500K x 4% = $20K — insufficient
Bubble Ads Promotional Plan: $650K x 4% = $26K — meets target
Krab Kard Rewards Program: $800K x 2% = $16K — insufficient
math.answer: Recommend the Bubble Ads Promotional Plan, which yields $26K in revenue this year, closing the $25K gap and bringing total revenue to $751K.

brainstorming.prompt: What strategies can Mr. Krabs use to create revenue synergies between the Krunchy Krab, Flying Dutchman Fries, and Patrick's Pizza?

categories.name: Price
ideas: Sell products in combination deals / bundling (e.g., burger + fries + pizza slice)
Use shared marketing channels to improve brand recognition across all three restaurants
Introduce new, complementary products at each restaurant that leverage the combined menu

categories.name: Volume
ideas: Leverage increased pricing power from combined brand to raise product prices
Run cross-restaurant promotions and discounts to drive foot traffic
Introduce a shared rewards program for visits and purchases across all three locations

recommendation: Given Mr. Krabs' short-term growth goals, the Krunchy Krab should focus on inorganic growth by acquiring Flying Dutchman Fries and Patrick's Pizza to add $225K in additional sales at a combined cost of $300K (within the $400K budget)
Capture the remaining $25K revenue gap by launching a 'Bubble Ads' shared billboard promotional initiative for the combined restaurant group, generating an estimated $26K in revenue this year
This two-pronged strategy brings total projected revenue to approximately $751K, meeting Mr. Krabs' $750K target
risks: Mergers don't always result in synergies, so the Krunchy Krab might still fall short of Mr. Krabs' target sales goal, especially within such a short timeline
Competitive response from the Clam Bucket — Plankton might respond by acquiring another restaurant or growing organically
Cultural integration issues between the three restaurants could slow execution
Cannibalization risk — acquired restaurants may simply steal customers from one another rather than add new sales to the group
The acquired restaurants might carry hidden debt — risk of insufficient due diligence given the short timeline
Overemphasis on short-term market share gain might not lead to long-term prosperity or sustainable competitive advantage
next_steps: Initiate negotiations for acquiring Flying Dutchman Fries and Patrick's Pizza and begin integration planning
Contact marketing team to start promotional planning for the shared Bubble Ads billboard campaign
Conduct proper due diligence on both acquisition targets to uncover any hidden liabilities
